item.title: Mauritania: Suivi des Mouvements de Transhumance (TTT), Mauritanie - Wilayas du Guidimagha et Hodh Ech Chargui - Alerte, Tableau de Bord 2, Collecte de données : avril, mai et juin 2026, Date de publication : septembre 2026
item.description:
Country: Mauritania
Source: International Organization for Migration

Please refer to the attached file.

Afin de promouvoir une transhumance apaisée, l’OIM a mis en œuvre, depuis 2019, l’outil de suivi des mouvements de transhumance (Transhumance Tracking Tool en anglais). Ce dispositif intègre une composante de système d’alerte précoce (SAP), permettant de recueillir des informations sur les événements (conflits et catastrophes) ainsi que sur les mouvements massifs, soudains et inhabituels de bétail. Les alertes générées facilitent la prévention des conflits et la gestion des aléas naturels, notamment les feux de brousse, qu’ils soient d’origine naturelle ou anthropique, contribuant ainsi à en atténuer les impacts. Afin d'assurer l'efficacité de l’outil TTT, celui-ci est mis en œuvre en collaboration avec le Groupement National des Associations Pastorales (GNAP). L'engagement du GNAP, acteur clé du secteur pastoral, facilite le déclenchement rapide d'alertes face aux menaces telles que la sécheresse, les maladies animales, les épidémies et les conflits agropastoraux.

Sur la période d’avril à juin, le système d’alerte a enregistré 46 alertes. Parmi celles-ci, 26 étaient liées à des mouvements, soit 57 pour cent, tandis que 20 alertes concernaient des événements, soit 43 pour cent. Sur les wilayas couvertes par le système d’alerte, Hodh ech Chargui a enregistré 56 pour cent d’alertes liées aux mouvements, contre 44 pour cent relatives aux événements. En revanche, au Guidimagha, 57 pour cent des alertes concernaient des mouvements, tandis que 43 pour cent étaient associées à des événements.

item.title: Country Update - Mauritania July 2026
item.description:
Countries: Mauritania, Mali
Source: UN High Commissioner for Refugees

Please refer to the attached file.

Mauritania is one of the principal refugee-hosting countries in West Africa. As of July 2026, the country hosts an estimated 305,000 refugees and asylum-seekers, the overwhelming majority of whom have fled insecurity and conflict in neighbouring Mali. While most refugees are concentrated in the region of Hodh Chargui in the southeast, a number of refugees and asylum-seekers also reside in urban areas, particularly Nouakchott and Nouadhibou. Hodh Chargui hosts approximately 290,000 refugees and asylum-seekers, representing over a third of the region's population. Established in 2012 and located in Hodh Chargui, Mbera Camp currently hosts around 120,000 refugees, while more than 170,000 live among host communities across the region. The volatile security situation in Mali continues to drive new arrivals. In this context, UNHCR and partners remain prepared to respond to further influxes while supporting the Mauritanian Government in strengthening inclusive systems and equitable access to protection and essential services At the same time, urban areas play an increasingly important role in Mauritania's forced displacement context. Currently, close to 14,000 refugees and asylum-seekers are living in Nouakchott and Nouadhibou, including refugees from Mali and 47 other nationalities. These cities are also key transit points for mixed movements towards North Africa and Europe. In line with its country strategy, UNHCR supports the Government in refugee registration and refugee status determination (RSD), while providing protection and promoting solutions for refugees and asylum-seekers.

KEY HIGHLIGHTS

• The Islamic Republic of Mauritania faces significant challenges related to land degradation and desertification, with vast portions of its territory being arid and only 0.4 percent of land classified as arable. Desertification drastically reduces soil fertility and productive capacity, negatively impacting both agricultural and pastoral livelihoods.

• According to the November 2025 Cadre Harmonisé analysis’ projections, 612,395 people people (12 percent of the population) could face crisis-or higher- level of food insecurity during the ongoing lean season (June–September), with Hodh Chargui (HEC) being the regions with the highest rates. In HEC alone, 46,268 in-camp refugees and 66,038 out-of-camp refugees are currently projected in phase 3+ for the 2026 lean season.

item.title: Mauritania: Mauritanie — Etude sur la vulnérabilité climatique (Décembre 2025 – Janvier 2026)
item.description:
Country: Mauritania
Source: International Organization for Migration

Please refer to the attached file.

L'Organisation Internationale pour les Migrations (OIM) en Mauritanie a déployé une évaluation de la vulnérabilité climatique (en anglais, Climate Vulnerability Assessment- CVA) de la Matrice de Suivi des Déplacements (en anglais, Displacement Tracking Matrix DTM) pour évaluer la vulnérabilité des localités aux déplacements induits par le climat.

Cet outil s'articule autour de quatre dimensions : les aléas environnementaux et l'accès à l'eau, les services et les infrastructures, les moyens de subsistance et les mesures d'atténuation, et enfin les tensions et les conflits. La collecte de données s'est déroulée du 13 décembre 2025 au 2 janvier 2026, couvrant deux wilayas, le Hodh Chargui et le Guidimakha, six moughataas et 196 localités.

Les 196 localités couvertes font apparaître un lien entre mobilité et vulnérabilité qui ne se réduit pas à l'association habituelle entre déplacement et détresse. Dans l'échantillon, la mobilité apparaît moins comme une mesure de la vulnérabilité que comme un facteur qui la module.

item.title: Mauritania: MSF assists migrants in distress who disembarked on West African shores
item.description:
Countries: Mauritania, Côte d'Ivoire, Gambia, Guinea, Mali, Senegal, World
Source: Médecins Sans Frontières
  • During the last week of August, MSF teams in Mauritania and Senegal assisted people who had disembarked from boats attempting to cross to the Canary Islands.
  • Our support included providing medical care, essential items, and emergency mental health care.
  • West African and European governments must put in place safe and legal pathways for migration.

Dakar, Senegal – A total of 1,046 people who survived attempted boat crossings on the Atlantic migration route disembarked in a vulnerable condition during the last week of August at three West African cities: Nouadhibou in Mauritania, and Rosso and Dakar in Senegal.

The survivors were onboard seven boats in distress that had departed from The Gambia and were heading for the Canary Islands, in the Atlantic Ocean — one of the longest migration routes in the world — before becoming stranded at sea. They were rescued and brought to shore, where Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) medical teams provided them with emergency medical support in collaboration with the Mauritanian Red Crescent in Nouadhibou and with the International Organization for Migration in Rosso and Dakar.

They were suffering from medical conditions that included extreme dehydration, unconsciousness, bone fractures, extreme fatigue, and skin, gastric and respiratory infections from being stranded for an extended period of time at sea. The survivors included 134 women, including one who is pregnant, and 88 minors in need of protection.

Most survivors came from Senegal and The Gambia; others came from Mali, Guinea, and Côte d'Ivoire. Many told our team that they had suffered violence in their country of origin as well as along the migration route. One survivor who disembarked in Dakar said that he was beaten by a smuggler and unidentified men to force him to pay more money for the crossing. A female survivor told our team that a smuggler took her crossing payment and then raped her ahead of boarding the boat.

“When people take a 2,000-kilometre route that is currently the deadliest in the world, they must be escaping something worse,” says Dalil Adji, head of mission for MSF’s migration task force in West Africa. “People we support frequently tell our teams that they took the route to escape violence and extreme conditions in their country of origin, only to be met with more violence along the way.”

We call on the governments of West Africa and Europe to prevent this human toll by putting in place safe and legal pathways for people to seek safety...

Dalil Adji, head of mission for MSF’s migration task force in West Africa

“We call on the governments of West Africa and Europe to prevent this human toll by putting in place safe and legal pathways for people to seek safety, and by creating a migration response that prioritises human life, dignity, and timely assistance,” says Adji.

In addition to providing emergency medical support, MSF teams referred severe cases for specialised medical care and provided survivors with water, food, blankets, and dignity kits, as well as emergency mental health care.

Our teams have been assisting people who disembark from distressed boats from the Atlantic route since 2024. From the launch of the project, MSF teams have been bearing witness to the growing human toll of this migration route, and the level of vulnerability among those who take it. Despite the evident dangers, people continue to take this risky route for lack of alternatives.

item.title: Mauritania: DTM Mauritanie — Aperçu des déplacements de population et des besoins humanitaires - Hodh Ech Chargui (juin 2026)
item.description:
Countries: Mauritania, Mali
Source: International Organization for Migration

Please refer to the attached file.

Ce rapport fournit un aperçu des retours et des besoins humanitaires multisectoriels dans les localités d'accueil des personnes retournées mauritaniennes du Mali. Les résultats ont été obtenus après la conduite du premier cycle de l'évaluation multisectorielle des localités (MSLA, round 1), réalisé du 16 au 28 juin 2026 par l'Organisation internationale pour les migrations (OIM) grâce au soutien du mécanisme de financement flexible de l'OIM (Flexible Funding Mechanism), avec l'appui des autorités administratives locales. L'évaluation a couvert 151 localités d'accueil des retournés, identifiées préalablement avec les autorités locales, dans cinq moughataas de la wilaya du Hodh Ech Chargui (Bassikounou, Adelbagrou, Amourj, Djigueni et Timbedra). Les données ont été collectées au moyen d'un questionnaire structuré multisectoriel, administré en français et en arabe au niveau des localités, auprès d'informateurs clés incluant des représentants des retournés (46%), des chefs de village (34%) et des leaders communautaires (15%).

item.title: WFP Mauritania Country Brief, August 2026
item.description:
Countries: Mauritania, Mali
Source: World Food Programme

Please refer to the attached file.

SITUATION OVERVIEW

• Mauritania hosts the largest number of Malian refugees in West Africa, Mauritania provides protection to almost 309,000 refugees, including 14,402 newly arrivals in Hodh Chargui (HEC) between October 2025 and May 2026. Of these new arrivals, 20 percent are women and 68 percent are children. WFP continues to provide life-saving food and nutrition assistance to refugees and host communities in HEC, adapting its response to increasing humanitarian needs.

• Mauritania’s heavy reliance on food and fuel imports has heightened its exposure to the crisis in the Middle East and Gulf region, prompting a fourth fuel price increase since March, most recently in June. This increases transportation costs and contributes to higher prices for food and other essential commodities, especially in remote and inland regions. WFP continues to monitor the potential implications for operational costs, market dynamics, and food security.

• In response to forecasts of below-average rainfall and a heightened risk of drought associated with the El Niño phenomenon in several regions, the Government triggered anticipatory actions for the first time. Assistance was officially launched with humanitarian partners, including WFP, on 26 July.

item.title: Mauritania: MSF deeply shocked after witnessing the recent fatal crossing on the Atlantic migration route
item.description:
Country: Mauritania
Source: Médecins Sans Frontières

Nouadhibou, Mauritania, 22 July 2026 — Médecins Sans Frontières/Doctors Without Borders (MSF) is deeply alarmed by a deadly incident on the Atlantic migration route, following the disembarkation in Nouadhibou of survivors from a boat that reportedly departed from The Gambia towards the Canary Islands. ​

According to initial testimonies collected from survivors, around 190 people were on board the boat. After 25 days at sea, only 38 people survived. The survivors were first assisted by fishermen, then by the Mauritanian coastguards, before being brought to the Mauritanian Red Crescent, which requested MSF’s support.

This is one of the deadliest disembarkations witnessed by MSF teams in Mauritania since the beginning of 2026. This event is a stark reminder of the extreme dangers faced by people attempting to take the Atlantic route, where crossings are often long, perilous, and marked by risks of shipwreck, dehydration, violence, severe psychological trauma and, above all, loss of life.

In recent weeks, MSF teams in Nouadhibou supported three disembarkation interventions, on 14 and 18 July, assisting a total of 387 people. MSF teams carried out 66 medical consultations and referred nine people to specialised health facilities in Nouadhibou. On 18 July alone, MSF responded to two successive disembarkations between midnight and 7 p.m., one of which followed the deadly incident involving the boat that had departed from The Gambia. People who reached the shore were suffering from post-traumatic shock and psychosis, bone fractures, traumatic injuries, and hypothermia.

Survivors described terrifying conditions at sea, as well as the loss of relatives and other passengers during the crossing. MSF teams observed acute psychological distress among survivors. The severity of the testimonies and the scale of the loss of life also had a significant psychological impact on the teams involved in the response.

“What our teams saw in Nouadhibou is deeply shocking. People arrived after weeks spent at sea, exhausted, traumatised and grieving the loss of relatives and other passengers who did not survive the crossing. One of the 38 survivors cared for by MSF said she had seen her sister die before her eyes. No one should have to endure such suffering while seeking safety or dignity,” says Fouzia Bara, MSF migration programme manager.

The Atlantic migration route has become one of the deadliest in the world. According to the Spanish NGO Caminando Fronteras, almost 10,000 people were reported dead or missing while attempting the Atlantic crossing in 2024, and almost 2,000 in 2025. It is very likely that the actual number of people who have died is higher than the reported figures, as not all sea crossings are reported or lead to rescues. Although arrivals to the Canary Islands have decreased this year, the risks remain extreme. According to UNHCR, arrivals to the Spanish archipelago have decreased by 61 per cent compared with 2025, with 4,400 arrivals recorded as of 15 July. Yet recent incidents underline the persistent dangers faced by refugees and migrants attempting to reach Europe, many of whom depart from points located more than 2,000 kilometres from their intended destination.

MSF launched its “Atlantic Migration” project in Mauritania following the increase in tragedies at sea. In Nouadhibou, MSF began providing direct assistance during disembarkations and interceptions in December 2024, before strengthening its response with the opening of the Centre for Reception, Care and Assistance — CASA in April 2025. The centre supports the most vulnerable people, whether they are migrants, in transit, or of Mauritanian origin.

MSF calls for urgent measures to prevent further deaths on the Atlantic route. Search and rescue mechanisms must be strengthened, adequately resourced, and able to respond effectively to the needs of people in distress at sea. At the same time, safe and legal pathways are needed to reduce the risks people are forced to take when seeking protection, safety or a better future.

“The deaths of these men, women and children must not be met with silence. MSF calls on governments and relevant authorities to place the preservation of human life at the centre of their migration policies, to strengthen search and rescue capacities, and to ensure that no person in distress at sea is left without assistance,” added Fouzia Bara.

MSF urges governments of countries along the migration route, European states, and regional and international actors to work collectively to prevent further loss of life. Saving lives at sea and ensuring humane and dignified assistance to survivors must be an immediate priority.

item.title: Mauritania: L'OIM consternée par le naufrage le plus meurtrier de migrants sur la route migratoire atlantique de l’Afrique de l’Ouest en 2026
item.description:
Countries: Mauritania, World
Source: International Organization for Migration

Nouakchott, 22 juillet 2026 – L'Organisation internationale pour les migrations (OIM) est profondément consternée par les informations faisant état de dizaines de migrants morts ou portés disparus à la suite d'un naufrage au large des côtes mauritaniennes, où 38 survivants ont été secourus par les garde-côtes mauritaniens près de Nouadhibou le 18 juillet.

Selon les survivants, l'embarcation avait quitté la Gambie avec environ 180 personnes à bord et a passé 25 jours en mer avant que les opérations de secours ne soient déclenchées par les garde-côtes mauritaniens et des pêcheurs locaux. Les survivants comprennent des hommes, des femmes et des enfants originaires de plusieurs pays d'Afrique de l'Ouest. Un corps a été récupéré ; au moins 143 personnes sont portées disparues et sont présumées avoir péri au cours du voyage. Parmi les survivants se trouvent deux enfants qui auraient perdu leurs parents et leur jeune frère ou sœur durant cette tragique traversée.

L'OIM présente ses plus sincères condoléances aux familles des victimes et exprime sa gratitude aux autorités mauritaniennes, aux communautés de pêcheurs locaux et à tous les premiers intervenants ayant participé à l'opération de secours.

« Chaque vie perdue sur cette route est une vie de trop. Mes pensées accompagnent les familles en deuil, ainsi que les survivants qui ont enduré une épreuve inimaginable », a déclaré Sylvia Ekra, Directrice régionale de l'OIM pour l'Afrique de l'Ouest et centrale.

Cette tragédie s'ajoute aux 168 vies déjà perdues sur la route migratoire atlantique de l’Afrique de l’Ouest vers les Canaries cette année, ainsi qu'à deux naufrages invisibles présumés, encore en cours de vérification, qui pourraient avoir coûté la vie à des centaines de personnes supplémentaires.

Pour la seule année en cours, 4 440 arrivées ont été enregistrées aux îles Canaries, contre 11 575 entre janvier et juillet de l'année dernière, ce qui démontre que la baisse du nombre d'arrivées ne signifie pas que la route est devenue plus sûre.

« Ce que cet incident révèle, c'est qu'une diminution des arrivées ne signifie pas que la route est devenue plus sûre. Les personnes continuent de tout risquer parce que les pressions qui poussent à ces voyages demeurent. Sauver des vies exige un effort collectif qui va au-delà des opérations de recherche et de sauvetage. Nous avons besoin d'une coopération renforcée tout au long de la route, des pays d'origine aux pays de transit et de destination, avec un investissement accru dans la protection, des opportunités plus proches de chez soi et un accès élargi à des voies de migration sûres et régulières », a déclaré Sylvia Ekra de l'OIM.

Cet incident souligne l'urgence d'un renforcement de la coopération régionale et d'efforts soutenus pour prévenir de nouvelles pertes en vies humaines le long des routes migratoires à travers l'Afrique de l'Ouest et du Nord-Ouest.

Pour plus d'informations, veuillez consulter le Centre médias de l'OIM.

item.title: Mauritania: La OIM expresa su consternación por el naufragio de migrantes más mortífero en la ruta atlántica de África Occidental en 2026
item.description:
Countries: Mauritania, World
Source: International Organization for Migration

Nuakchot, 22 de julio de 2026 – La Organización Internacional para las Migraciones (OIM) expresa su profunda consternación ante los informes que indican que decenas de migrantes han muerto o están desaparecidos tras un naufragio frente a las costas de Mauritania, donde 38 sobrevivientes fueron rescatados por la Guardia Costera mauritana cerca de Nuadibú el 18 de julio.

Según los sobrevivientes, la embarcación partió de Gambia con aproximadamente 180 personas a bordo y estuvo 25 días en el mar antes de que las guardacostas mauritanas y los pescadores locales iniciaran las labores de rescate. Entre los sobrevivientes se encuentran hombres, mujeres y niños procedentes de varios países de África Occidental. Se recuperó el cuerpo de una persona fallecida; al menos 143 personas permanecen desaparecidas y se teme que hayan perdido la vida durante el trayecto. Entre los sobrevivientes hay dos niños que, según los testimonios, perdieron a sus padres y a un hermano menor durante el trágico viaje.

La OIM expresa sus más sinceras condolencias a las familias de quienes perdieron la vida y manifiesta su gratitud a las autoridades mauritanas, a las comunidades de pescadores locales y a todos los equipos de primera respuesta que participaron en la operación de rescate.

"Cada vida perdida en esta ruta es una vida de más. Mi pensamiento está con las familias que lloran a sus seres queridos y con los sobrevivientes que han soportado una experiencia inimaginable", declaró Sylvia Ekra, Directora Regional de la OIM para África Occidental y Central.

Esta tragedia se suma a las 168 vidas ya perdidas en la ruta atlántica de África Occidental hacia las Canarias este año, así como a dos naufragios presuntos aún no verificados que permanecen en proceso de verificación y que podrían haber cobrado cientos de vidas más.

Solo en lo que va de año, se han registrado 4.440 llegadas a las Islas Canarias, frente a las 11.575 contabilizadas de enero a julio del año pasado, lo que demuestra que la disminución de las llegadas no significa que la ruta se haya vuelto más segura.

"Lo que este incidente pone de manifiesto es que una disminución de las llegadas no significa que la ruta se haya vuelto más segura. Las personas siguen arriesgándolo todo porque las presiones que impulsan estos viajes persisten. Salvar vidas exige un esfuerzo colectivo que va más allá de la búsqueda y el rescate. Necesitamos una cooperación más sólida a lo largo de toda la ruta, desde los países de origen hasta los países de tránsito y de destino, con una mayor inversión en protección, oportunidades más cercanas al hogar y un acceso ampliado a vías de migración regular y segura", afirmó Ekra, de la OIM.

Esta tragedia subraya la necesidad urgente de reforzar la cooperación regional y mantener los esfuerzos para prevenir nuevas pérdidas de vidas humanas en las rutas migratorias de África Occidental y Noroccidental.

Para más información, visite el Centro de Prensa de la OIM.

item.title: Mauritania: IOM Saddened by Deadliest Migrant Shipwreck on West African Atlantic Route in 2026
item.description:
Countries: Mauritania, World
Source: International Organization for Migration

Nouakchott, 22 July 2026 – The International Organization for Migration (IOM) is deeply saddened by reports that dozens of migrants are dead or missing following a shipwreck off the coast of Mauritania, where 38 survivors were rescued by the Mauritanian Coast Guard near Nouadhibou on 18 July.

According to survivors, the vessel departed from The Gambia carrying approximately 180 people and spent 25 days at sea before rescue efforts were launched by Mauritanian coast guards and local fishermen. The survivors include men, women and children from several West African countries. One deceased person was recovered; at least 143 people are missing and are feared to have perished during the journey. Among the survivors are two children who reportedly lost their parents and younger sibling during the tragic journey.

IOM extends its heartfelt condolences to the families of those who lost their lives and expresses its gratitude to the Mauritanian authorities, local fishing communities and all first responders involved in the rescue operation.

"Every life lost on this route is one life too many. My thoughts are with the families who are mourning loved ones, and with the survivors who have endured an unimaginable ordeal," said Sylvia Ekra, IOM Regional Director for West and Central Africa.

This tragedy adds to the 168 lives already lost on the West African Atlantic Route to the Canaries this year, as well as two suspected invisible shipwrecks that remain under verification and may have claimed hundreds more lives.

This year alone, 4,440 arrivals have been recorded in the Canary Islands compared with 11,575 from January to July last year, demonstrating that the decrease in arrivals does not mean the route has become safer.

"What this incident shows is that a decline in arrivals does not mean the route has become safer. People continue to risk everything because the pressures that drive these journeys remain. Saving lives requires a collective effort that goes beyond search and rescue. We need stronger cooperation all along the route, from countries of origin to countries of transit and destination, with greater investment in protection, opportunities closer to home, and expanded access to safe and regular pathways", said IOM’s Ekra.

The incident underscores the urgent need for strengthened regional cooperation and sustained efforts to prevent further loss of life along migration routes across West and Northwest Africa.

For more information, please visit IOM’s Media Centre.

item.title: Mauritania: المفوضية السامية للأمم المتحدة لشؤون اللاجئين تشعر بحزن عميق إثر تقارير عن وفاة أو فقدان 144 شخصاً قبالة سواحل غرب إفريقيا | مفوضية اللاجئين
item.description:
Countries: Mauritania, Gambia, Spain, World
Source: UN High Commissioner for Refugees

جنيف – أعربت المفوضية السامية للأمم المتحدة لشؤون اللاجئين (UNHCR) عن بالغ حزنها وقلقها إزاء التقارير التي تفيد بوفاة أو فقدان 144 شخصاً نتيجة حادث مأساوي عرض البحار وقع قبالة سواحل موريتانيا الأسبوع الماضي.

وأُفادت التقارير بأن اللاجئين والمهاجرين لقوا حتفهم أو فُقدوا خلال قيامهم برحلة بحرية محفوفة بالمخاطر من غرب إفريقيا باتجاه أوروبا، في ما يسلّط الضوء مجدداً على الكلفة الإنسانية الباهظة المرتبطة بهذه المسارات الخطرة.

وفي المجمل، تمّت ثلاث عمليات إنقاذ وإنزال بين 14 و18 يوليو/تموز في مدينة نواذيبو الموريتانية، وصل خلالها 387 شخصاً بسلام إلى اليابسة. وكانت المفوضية حاضرة خلال جميع عمليات الإنزال إلى جانب السلطات الوطنية والشركاء الإنسانيين، لتقديم الدعم للناجين وتحديد الأشخاص الأكثر عرضة للمخاطر ممن قد يحتاجون إلى حماية دولية.

وينحدر الناجون من عدة دول من إفريقيا الغربية.

وقد عاش ركاب أحد القوارب التي تم إنقاذها في 18 يوليو/تموز مأساة مروعة، حيث تم الإبلاغ عن فقدان أو وفاة 143 شخصاً، فيما نجا 38 شخصاً فقط بعد أن ظلوا تائهين في المحيط الأطلسي لما يقرب من 25 يوماً إثر مغادرتهم منطقة بوفالوتو في غامبيا في محاولة للوصول إلى إسبانيا. وكان من بين الناجين طفلان فقدا جميع أفراد أسرتهما خلال الرحلة ويتلقيان حالياً الرعاية في المستشفى إلى جانب ناجين آخرين.

كما تم الإبلاغ عن وفاة شخص آخر كان على متن قارب أُنزل ركابه إلى اليابسة في 14 يوليو/تموز.

ويُعد هذا تذكيراً صارخاً بأنه، رغم الجهود المتواصلة التي تبذلها السلطات والشركاء الإنسانيون لإنقاذ الأرواح، فإن الطريق البحري الأطلسي الممتد من غرب إفريقيا نحو جزر الكناري يُعد أحد أكثر ممرات الهجرة المختلطة فتكاً في العالم، نظراً لطول المسافات وتقلب الأحوال البحرية واستخدام قوارب غير صالحة للإبحار ومكتظة بالركاب، إضافة إلى محدودية عمليات الإنقاذ في حالات الطوارئ.

ورغم انخفاض أعداد الزوارق التي وصلت إلى أرخبيل جزر الكناري الإسباني خلال العام الجاري بنسبة 61 في المائة مقارنة بعام 2025، ليبلغ 4,400 وافد حتى 15 يوليو/تموز، فإن هذه الحوادث تؤكد استمرار المخاطر التي يواجهها اللاجئون والمهاجرون الساعون للوصول إلى أوروبا والذين ينطلق كثير منهم من نقاط تبعد أكثر من 2,000 كيلومتر عن وجهتهم المقصودة.

وبشكل عام، تجاوزت أعداد الوصول إلى أوروبا بحراً عبر المسارات الرئيسية 40 ألف شخص منذ بداية العام الجاري، مقارنة بـ65,407 شخص خلال النصف الأول من عام 2025. ومع ذلك، دأبت المفوضية وشركاؤها على التحذير من أن أعداد الوفيات وحالات الفقدان في البحر لا تزال مرتفعة بشكل مقلق، حيث تقع العديد من الحوادث بعيداً عن أنظار الرأي العام وغالباً ما تؤدي إلى اختفاء قوارب بأكملها.

وفي هذا السياق، تُظهر عمليات الإنقاذ في موريتانيا الحاجة إلى بذل جهود منسقة لمعالجة الأسباب الجذرية التي تدفع اللاجئين والمهاجرين إلى خوض هذه الرحلات الخطرة، إلى جانب توفير سبل أكثر جدوى وأسرع للوصول إلى المسارات القانونية من خلال زيادة في أعداد المستفيدين من برامج إعادة التوطين وتوفير فرص العمل وإتاحة المزيد من مسارات التعليم كبدائل لعبور البحر المحفوف بالمخاطر.

وحتى الآن في عام 2026، تم تسجيل 17 عملية إنزال في كل من نواذيبو ونواكشوط، أفضت إلى إنقاذ 2,147 شخصاً.

item.title: Mauritania: ACNUR expresa su profunda consternación por la muerte o desaparición de 144 personas frente a las costas de África occidental
item.description:
Countries: Mauritania, Gambia, Spain, World
Source: UN High Commissioner for Refugees

GINEBRA – La Agencia de la ONU para los Refugiados (ACNUR) ha expresado profunda consternación y preocupación ante las informaciones que apuntan a que 144 personas habrían muerto o desaparecido como consecuencia de varios accidentes marítimos ocurridos la semana pasada frente a las costas de Mauritania.

Las víctimas, entre ellas personas refugiadas y migrantes, intentaban alcanzar Europa por mar desde África occidental, una travesía extremadamente peligrosa que pone de nuevo de manifiesto el elevado coste humano de estas rutas.

Entre el 14 y el 18 de julio se llevaron a cabo tres operaciones de rescate y desembarco en Nuadibú, Mauritania, que permitieron poner a salvo a 387 personas. ACNUR estuvo presente en todas ellas junto a las autoridades nacionales y organizaciones humanitarias para asistir a las personas supervivientes e identificar a quienes pudieran necesitar protección internacional. Las personas rescatadas procedían de distintos países.

Uno de los episodios más trágicos afectó a una embarcación rescatada el 18 de julio. Según las informaciones disponibles, 143 personas murieron o permanecen desaparecidas y solo 38 sobrevivieron tras permanecer cerca de 25 días a la deriva en el Atlántico tras zarpar de Bufaloto, en Gambia, con destino a España. Entre las personas supervivientes hay dos menores que perdieron a todos sus familiares durante la travesía y que se recuperan en el hospital junto a otras personas rescatadas.

También se informó del fallecimiento de otra persona que viajaba en una embarcación cuyos ocupantes desembarcaron el 14 de julio.

Estos hechos recuerdan con crudeza que, pese a los esfuerzos sostenidos de las autoridades costeras y las organizaciones humanitarias por salvar vidas, la ruta atlántica entre África occidental y Canarias sigue siendo una de las más mortíferas del mundo. Las largas distancias, las condiciones imprevisibles del océano, las embarcaciones precarias y sobrecargadas y la dificultad para acceder a rescates a tiempo siguen haciendo de esta una de las rutas más letales.

Aunque las llegadas al archipiélago canario han caído un 61% respecto a 2025 y se situaban en 4.400 personas a 15 de julio, estos incidentes ponen de relieve los riesgos persistentes a los que se enfrentan las personas refugiadas y migrantes que intentan llegar a Europa, muchas de las cuales emprenden la travesía desde puntos situados a más de 2.000 kilómetros de su destino.

En conjunto, las principales rutas marítimas hacia Europa han registrado más de 40.000 llegadas en lo que va de año, frente a las 65.407 contabilizadas durante el primer semestre de 2025. Sin embargo, ACNUR y sus socios advierten de que las muertes y desapariciones en el mar continúan produciéndose a niveles alarmantes. Muchos de estos incidentes ocurren lejos de la atención pública y, en algunos casos, terminan con embarcaciones enteras desapareciendo sin dejar rastro.

En este contexto, los rescates llevados a cabo en Mauritania ponen de manifiesto la necesidad de redoblar los esfuerzos para abordar las causas profundas que empujan a las personas refugiadas y migrantes a emprender estas peligrosas travesías. Al mismo tiempo, resulta imprescindible facilitar un mayor y más rápido acceso a vías legales, mediante un aumento de las plazas de reasentamiento, más oportunidades de movilidad laboral y vías de acceso a la educación como alternativas a los peligrosos cruces marítimos.

En lo que va de 2026 se han registrado 17 operaciones de desembarco en Nuadibú y Nuakchot, donde han sido rescatadas un total de 2.147 personas.

item.title: Mauritania: UNHCR deeply saddened as 144 people reportedly dead or missing off West Africa
item.description:
Countries: Mauritania, World
Source: UN High Commissioner for Refugees

GENEVA – UNHCR, the UN Refugee Agency, is extremely saddened and concerned at reports that 144 people are either dead or missing as a result of tragic maritime incidents off the coast of Mauritania last week.

The refugees and migrants were reported dead or missing after attempting the perilous sea journey from West Africa towards Europe, highlighting the continued human cost of these dangerous routes.

Overall, three rescue and disembarkation operations were conducted between 14 and 18 July in Nouadhibou, Mauritania, which brought 387 people safely ashore. UNHCR was present at all disembarkations alongside national authorities and humanitarian partners to support survivors and identify vulnerable individuals seeking international protection. Survivors came from various countries.

Passengers on one of the boats rescued on 18 July had experienced particular tragedy, with 143 people reported missing or dead and just 38 surviving after nearly 25 days stranded on the Atlantic after departing from Bufaloto, The Gambia, in an attempt to reach Spain. Among the survivors were two children, who had lost all their family members during the journey and are now recovering in hospital with other survivors.

Another death was reported among passengers on a boat that was disembarked on 14 July.

This is a stark reminder that, despite sustained efforts by coastal authorities and humanitarian partners to save lives, the Atlantic route from West Africa towards the Canary Islands remains one of the world's deadliest mixed movement corridors due to long distances, unpredictable ocean conditions, unseaworthy overcrowded boats and limited access to timely rescue.

Despite the number of arrivals to the Spanish archipelago dropping this year – by 61 per cent from 2025, with 4,400 arrivals as of 15 July – the incidents highlight the persistent risks faced by refugees and migrants attempting to reach Europe, many of whom are embarking over 2,000 km away from their intended destination.

Overall, arrivals to Europe by sea on the major routes are over 40,000 this year compared to 65,407 in the first half of 2025. Still, UNHCR and partners have repeatedly warned that deaths and disappearances at sea continue at alarming levels, with many incidents occurring far from public attention and often resulting in entire boats vanishing.

Against this backdrop, the rescues in Mauritania demonstrate that concerted efforts need to be made to address the root causes driving refugees and migrants to take these perilous journeys, while providing meaningful and quicker access to legal pathways through higher resettlement quotas, increased labour opportunities and education pathways as alternatives to the dangerous sea crossings.

So far in 2026, 17 disembarkations have been recorded in Nouadhibou and Nouakchott, with a total of 2,147 individuals rescued.
